newsitem.title: INDIA: India encourages deep water search for oil.
newsitem.headline: India encourages deep water search for oil.

text.p: India needs to increase oil exploration efforts urgently to offset a steep increase in dependence on petroleum imports during the coming years, Sanjiv Mishra, ministry of petroleum joint secretary, said on Monday.

"On the assumption of a growth rate of gross domestic product of around seven percent over the next five years the annual growth rate in demand for petroleum products is expected to be in the region of 7.5 to 8.0 percent, he told the "India Oil and Gas Review" symposium.
Domestic crude oil production was expected to be around 35 million tonnes a year for the next few years, he said. Current petroleum consumption is around 80 million tonnes a year.

"Demand for natural gas is expected to be around 150 million cubic metres a day by the end of the century," he said. "Production is only likely to be half the amount at around 75 million cubic metres."
Oil and gas account for around 40 percent of India's total energy consumption.
"India urgently needs to step up exploration efforts," Mishra said.
"Thus the huge potential exists for expanding exploration... especially in deep water areas where virtually no work has begun so far," he said.

He also said there was need to improve the recovery rate from Indian oilfields, which at 28 percent was well below international average. Latest technology was required for better reservoir management and enhanced oil recovery techniques, he said.
